item.title: Synergistic Electronic‐Ionic Regulation in LMFP Cathodes Enabled by Mn‐Vacancy Engineering and D–p Orbital Hybridization
item.description:

Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in coupling Mn-vacancy engineering with Zn/Zr-induced d–p orbital hybridization to simultaneously boost ionic and electronic transport in LMFP cathodes. This synergistic electronic-ionic regulation lowers the band gap, enhances electron delocalization, and reduces Li⁺ diffusion barriers, yielding high capacity (156.8 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.2 C), excellent rate performance, and long cycling stability, establishing a general design strategy for olivine cathodes.

item.description:

ACS Nano | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an interfacial-selective electrochemical SEI decomposition (ESD) strategy that removes unstable organic SEI and rebuilds a thin inorganic-rich layer, restoring Li+ transport without bulk damage. Its significance: direct regeneration of spent graphite anodes while preserving the full electrode architecture, enabling low-energy, sustainable recycling with near-complete capacity recovery and improved cycling stability in both half and full cells.

💡 The novelty lies in showing metal–pore matching, not pore size alone, governs low-voltage alkali storage in nanoporous carbon, with distinct ionic–metallic filling mechanisms for Li, Na, and K. Significance: this enables metal-specific pore design, achieving capacities beyond graphite limits and guiding hard-carbon anode optimization beyond one-size-fits-all pore strategies.

ACS Nano | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in an iron-doping strategy creating a self-organized Fe₃O₄ shell on NASICON NTP, forming a bulk-shell dual-defense that suppresses titanate dissolution by consuming OH⁻ ions. This yields record capacity (164.9 mAh g⁻¹) with 90.9% retention over 2000 cycles and 106.4 Wh kg⁻¹ full-cell energy density, offering a broadly applicable approach for stabilizing electrodes in corrosive environments.
